⚠ Windows Server 2016 reaches End of Support on January 12, 2027

You're receiving this email because our records indicate your practice is still running Windows Server 2016.

We highly recommend planning your server replacement now. Server hardware often has lead times, so waiting until closer to the deadline could leave your practice without a plan in place before support ends.

Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support on January 12, 2027. After that date, Microsoft will stop providing security updates. This means your server will become classified as Unsupported Infrastructure, which could put your practice at risk of HIPAA fines and security vulnerabilities.

What is Windows Server 2016?

It's an operating system, similar to Windows 11, but built specifically for server hardware. It runs your network, data storage, and connected devices behind the scenes, rather than being the system on your everyday work computers.

Whether the right move is a server upgrade or a migration to the cloud, Darkhorse Tech can help you plan ahead as part of your HIPAA risk management process.

We also want to remind you that hardware pricing is still being affected by increased demand for AI infrastructure. The longer a replacement is delayed, the more a server upgrade is likely to cost. That's why our team is reaching out now to help you plan ahead.

We’re writing to let you know about an adjustment to the pricing of your IT support, cybersecurity, and HIPAA compliance services, effective January 1, 2027.

The threats facing dental practices changed noticeably this year. Attackers now use the same AI tools everyone else is adopting, and the results are showing up in practices like yours. campaigns.name: Security Advisory: AI Browser Agents and Your Dental Practice
campaigns.subject: Security Advisory: AI Browser Agents and Your Dental Practice
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
AI assistants can now browse websites and take action. Here's what your practice needs to know.

Security Advisory

AI Can Now Browse and Click for You. Is Your Practice Protected?

Artificial intelligence is moving beyond answering questions. New AI-powered browser assistants can navigate websites, fill out forms, download files, and perform tasks on your behalf.

For dental practices, that creates exciting possibilities—but also introduces new cybersecurity and patient privacy risks.

What makes these AI tools different?

Unlike traditional chatbots, AI browser agents may be able to interact with websites and applications where you're already signed in.

Depending on their permissions, these agents could:

  • Access patient information in practice management software, imaging applications, or insurance portals.
  • Perform actions using your login, including submitting information or changing records.
  • Expose confidential data to outside services through browser content, uploads, or automated actions.
  • Follow malicious instructions hidden inside websites or documents, potentially taking actions you never intended.

Four steps to protect your practice

1. Keep unapproved AI agents out of sensitive systems.

Do not use unapproved browser agents with Open Dental, Dentrix, Eaglesoft, imaging applications, patient communication systems, insurance portals, banking, or payroll.

2. Protect patient information.

Never enter or upload protected health information (PHI) into an AI tool that hasn't been properly reviewed and authorized. A vendor's Business Associate Agreement (BAA) alone does not guarantee that a particular workflow is appropriate.

3. Be cautious with AI browser extensions.

Before installing an AI assistant or granting it access to websites, consult your IT team. Simply closing sensitive browser tabs is not a reliable security control.

4. Keep humans involved.

Any AI automation that downloads patient records, changes information, or submits sensitive transactions should have appropriate access restrictions, oversight, and approval controls.

Does this mean your practice shouldn't use AI?

Absolutely not!

At Darkhorse Tech, we believe AI will fundamentally improve dental practice operations, from insurance verification and reporting to analytics and administrative automation.

The goal isn't to avoid AI. It's to adopt it safely.

Want to learn more?

Read our complete guide: AI Browser Agents Are Here. Is Your Dental Practice Using Them Safely?

Read the Complete Guide

If your team is considering a new AI assistant or automated workflow, contact Darkhorse Tech before connecting it to sensitive practice systems.

Darkhorse Tech
Your Partner in Dental IT, Cybersecurity, and AI Innovation

campaigns.name: Monthly HIPAA Compliance Update: Front Desk Verification
campaigns.subject: Monthly HIPAA Compliance Update: Front Desk Verification
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Hello,

Confirming who you are speaking with before sharing patient information is one of the simplest ways to protect privacy. Whether it happens at check-in, over the phone, or by email, verifying identity helps make sure information only goes to the patient or someone they have authorized.

What to do today:

• Verify identity before sharing or discussing patient information, using at least two identifiers such as full name and date of birth.
• Confirm that a caller or visitor is authorized before sharing details on a patient's behalf, such as a family member asking about an appointment or balance.
• Keep check-in and phone conversations quiet enough that others in the waiting area cannot overhear patient details.
• Let us know if you would like help putting a simple verification process in place for your front desk team.

We're here to help make sure your practice is fully HIPAA compliant. Reply to this email or open a support ticket to check up on your practice's HIPAA compliance.

campaigns.name: (copy 06)
campaigns.subject: Tropical Storm Isaias - How to Protect your Hardware
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Hello, you're receiving this email because your practice is located in or near the projected path of Tropical Storm Isaias, and we want to help you prepare. 
Projected path of Isaias, based on the NHC's Oct. 7 advisory. Times are Central. The forecast may change
We recomend you talk to our support team about your best options moving forward, but we also have provided some recomended steps to protect your IT equipment below:
Email Darkhorse Tech Support
Before the Storm:
  • Save open work and fully shut down computers, servers, and printers. Don't just put them to sleep. 
  • For your server, we have specific instructions below.
  • Unplug equipment from the wall, including surge protectors and battery backups (UPS)
     
After the Storm:
  • Don't power anything on if it got wet or if there is water in the office.
  • Once power is stable, turn on your network equipment (modem, firewall, switches) first, then servers, then workstations.
  • If anything isn't working as expected please reach out with a reply or open a support ticket and we'll help you get back up and running.

How to Safely Shut Down Your Server:
  1. Ensure all users are logged out of the server and any applications.
  2. At the server, press Ctrl + Alt + Delete.
  3. Select Shut Down from the menu.
  4. Wait until the server has completely powered off (no lights or fan noise).
⚠️ Do not unplug the server while it is running, as this can cause data loss or hardware issues.
 
How to Power the Server Back On:
Once power has been fully restored and is stable:
  1. Confirm internet and power are consistently available.
  2. Press the power button on the server once.
  3. Allow the server several minutes to fully boot.
  4. Once powered on, users may log back in as normal.
 
If You Need Assistance:
If you are unsure about any of these steps or experience issues after power is restored, please submit a support ticket or contact our team.
 
Please stay safe, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have questions or concerns.

-Darkhorse Tech Support

Hello,

If patient information is displayed on monitors or TVs, it should only be visible to authorized individuals. Be mindful of screen positioning, especially in operatories where others may be present. Simple adjustments can help prevent accidental exposure and support patient privacy.

What to do today:

• Avoid displaying patient information when not needed.
• Reposition screens if they can be seen from unintended areas, such as hallways or waiting rooms.

campaigns.name: Tam Email #8 (Jack)
campaigns.subject: AI Is Making Phishing Harder to Spot — Here's How to Stay Ahead
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
 

Hi << Test First Name >>, 
 

Healthcare is already one of the top targets for phishing and scam emails — you've probably seen an attempt land in your own inbox. What's changed is that attackers are now using AI to write polished, personalized messages that convincingly mimic a real colleague or vendor, making them much harder to catch at a glance.

The good news: most of the classic phishing rulebook still applies. Here's what to watch for, and how to stay protected.

How to Spot Them

  • Urgency — requests to reset a password, approve a payment, or "verify" an account right away.
  • Sender addresses — look closely, even when the display name looks right.
  • Unexpected links or attachments — be wary even when they appear to come from familiar names.

Steps to Protect Your Practice

  • Turn on multi-factor authentication everywhere it's available — it stops most account takeovers even if a password is stolen.
  • Make it easy to report — staff should feel comfortable flagging a suspicious email without hesitation.

What We Offer

Darkhorse Tech handles full setup of Ironscales on your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace — an email security platform that learns each employee's normal communication patterns and flags anything that deviates, including attacks from compromised but legitimate-looking accounts.

We also offer Huntress Security Awareness Training, which keeps your staff sharp with short, engaging lessons and simulated phishing tests based on real-world threats. It builds the habits that stop an attack before it starts, and gives you reporting to prove your team is trained and compliant.

campaigns.subject: How To Spot Phishing Emails
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Hello,

Phishing emails are one of the most common ways patient data gets exposed, and dental offices are a frequent target. A single click on the wrong link can put your whole practice at risk.

What a phishing email might look like:

Subject: Action Required: Invoice Payment Overdue
From: billing@dentaI-supplies-co.com

"Hi, your account balance is past due. Please review and pay the attached invoice immediately to avoid service interruption. Click here to view your invoice and update payment details."

Red flags: a sender domain that looks legitimate but is slightly altered (notice the capital "I" instead of a lowercase "l"), urgent language pushing immediate action, and a link or attachment asking for payment/login details.

What to do today:

• Remind your staff to slow down and verify before clicking links or downloading attachments, especially in emails asking for login credentials, payment info, or urgent action.
• Double-check the sender's email address on anything unexpected, even if it looks like it's from a known contact or vendor, since attackers often spoof familiar names.
• If you're using a compliance platform, confirm your team has completed (or is scheduled for) security awareness training that covers phishing recognition.
• Get support from Darkhorse if a suspicious email lands in an inbox or you're not sure whether something's legitimate. We're here to help you check it out before anyone clicks.

We're here to help make sure your practice is fully HIPAA compliant. Reply to this email or open a support ticket to check up on your practice's HIPAA compliance.

campaigns.name: TAM Email 2/5 - Hunter (Email 4)
campaigns.subject: It’s Crucial to Vet Your Vendors
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Hello << Test First Name >>, we wanted to share some useful information about third party vendors that could save your practice from some serious violations.
 

1. Who Are “Vendors”?

In a dental practice, vendors aren’t just supply reps. They’re the outside companies you bring in to run critical parts of your business. From IT support and marketing/website developers, to third-party apps that connect to your practice management system (PMS).

If they touch patient data, they’re part of your risk picture.

2. Why BAAs Matter (and Who’s Who)

Under HIPAA, a Covered Entity (CE) is your dental practice. A Business Associate (BA) is any vendor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits Protected Health Information (PHI) on your behalf.

That means:

  • You (the practice) are always on the hook for compliance.

  • Your vendor (the BA) must sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA), committing to safeguard PHI and flow those requirements down to any subcontractors.

💡 Pro tip: No signed BAA = 🚩. Without it, your practice carries the liability if there’s a breach.

3. The 3 Questions to Ask Every Vendor Before Hiring

  • Do you sign a BAA with the primary vendor—and can you provide a copy or confirmation? Why it matters: This proves they’re taking HIPAA obligations seriously,not leaving you exposed
  • Do you maintain independent cybersecurity protocols (MFA, encryption, etc.)? Why it matters: Multi-factor authentication and encryption are frontline defenses. If they don’t have them, your patient data may be a sitting duck.
  • What is your breach notification process and timeline? Why it matters: You don’t want to be the last to know when the fire alarm is already blaring. Quick notice = faster damage control.

✅ Bottom Line

Vetting vendors isn’t optional, it’s part of protecting your practice and your patients. Asking the right questions now can save you from headaches (and HIPAA penalties) later.

Reply to this email if you need assistance vetting any of your practices third party vendors.

Best,
Hunter Goulden
Territory Account Manager

campaigns.subject: Microsoft 365 vs Google: What’s Safer (and Cheaper) for Your Practice?
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Hello << Test First Name >>,

We at Darkhorse Tech have seen muliple environments for email security and compliance in Dental Offices. Here is a quick note as you compare email platforms.
In our opinion, Microsoft 365 is a stronger, more cost-effective choice than Google Workspace for dental practice that handle patient information.

Key Reasons:

  • Better protection: Microsoft includes stronger built‑in email threat protection and easier tools to keep patient info private.

  • Compliance made simple: Microsoft’s services and agreements fit HIPAA workflows more directly, reducing paperwork and risk.

  • Desktop apps: (Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams) All these make scheduling, chart access, and chairside use faster and more reliable. Online‑only Google apps can feel limited.

  • Easier device control: You can lock or wipe phones and tablets if lost, protecting patient records.

  • Smarter value: You often get needed security and productivity tools without buying expensive add‑ons, lowering total cost of ownership.

Likely monthly cost (per user) for HIPAA-cabale offerings:

  • Microsoft 365 Business Standard (core apps + email, no advanced device management): ~$12.50/user, ~$20/user with Email Encryption, Anti-Phishing, and MDR included.

  • Microsoft 365 Business Premium (includes advanced security, Intune): ~$20–$25/user.

  • Microsoft 365 E3 (larger practices needing advanced compliance): ~$32–$40/user.

  • Google Workspace Business Plus / Enterprise Essentials (to match security/compliance): $30+/user or additional paid security add‑ons.
     

For small‑to‑mid dental practices, Microsoft 365 Business Premium usually matches or beats Google’s total cost once you add the security and compliance features Google requires at higher tiers.

If you're evaluating email platforms, or just want a clearer comparison of your options, start a discussion with me!

Best,
Hunter Goulden

campaigns.subject: How Do You Know When It’s Time to Replace Your IT Equipment?
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Hello << Test First Name >>,

If you’re like most doctors we work with, replacing computers or servers isn’t high on your “fun purchases” list. Everything works ... until it doesn’t and then you’re dealing with downtime, stress, and unexpected costs.

The good news: most failures are predictable.

After supporting dental practices for over a decade, we’ve seen clear lifecycle patterns and wanted to share them with you:

- Workstations (Front Desk, Operatories, Offices)
Plan to replace around 5 years. After that, failure rates and slowdowns increase especially for imaging-connected computers (pano/CBCT), where downtime directly impacts patient care.

- Servers
Plan for replacement around 6 years. We recommend starting the conversation about 6 months in advance to ensure compatibility, proper sizing, and a smooth migration. Emergency server swaps are stressful. Planned ones are not.

- Networking Equipment (Firewall, Switches, Wi-Fi)
Reassess every 5–6 years to maintain strong security, reliable Wi-Fi, and performance that supports modern imaging and cloud systems.

Proactive replacement isn’t about buying hardware early. It’s about avoiding surprise downtime, protecting patient data, and budgeting intentionally instead of reacting to emergencies.

If you’re unsure how old your equipment is, we’re happy to help you map out a simple lifecycle plan. Send me a reply if you're interested.

The goal isn’t replacing things early.
It’s replacing them before they replace your schedule for the day.

Best,
Hunter Goulden

campaigns.subject: Inclement Weather Notice
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Hello,
 
Due to the potential for severe weather and possible power outages in your area, we want to share a few important reminders to help protect your systems and ensure a smooth recovery once power is restored.
 
Your safety comes first. Please take all necessary precautions to stay safe during the storm.
 
If You Experience a Power Outage:
If you are notified of an impending outage or notice unstable power, we recommend safely shutting down your server to prevent damage or data corruption.
 
How to Safely Shut Down Your Server:
  1. Ensure all users are logged out of the server and any applications.
  2. At the server, press Ctrl + Alt + Delete.
  3. Select Shut Down from the menu.
  4. Wait until the server has completely powered off (no lights or fan noise).
⚠️ Do not unplug the server while it is running, as this can cause data loss or hardware issues.
 
How to Power the Server Back On:
Once power has been fully restored and is stable:
  1. Confirm internet and power are consistently available.
  2. Press the power button on the server once.
  3. Allow the server several minutes to fully boot.
  4. Once powered on, users may log back in as normal.
 
If You Need Assistance:
If you are unsure about any of these steps or experience issues after power is restored, please submit a support ticket or contact our team. Response times may vary depending on weather conditions and overall impact, but we will assist as soon as possible.
 
Please stay safe, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have questions or concerns.

Cybercriminals are strategic. They do not attack at random, and they certainly do not take weekends or holidays off. Darkhorse Dental IT Monthly Newsletter
News & Resources for Dental Offices and DSOs
October 2025

News 

DSO & Multi-Office Dental IT Infrastructure Guide
Expanding from one dental practice to a growing network of locations—or a full DSO—introduces new layers of IT complexity. What once worked for a single site may now cause downtime, inconsistent performance, and compliance risk across your group. Complexity in these environments will mean more tickets for the support department down the road. Now is the time to stop, and plan out the typeof system you want.
Read the full article here: https://www.darkhorsetech.com/blogs/dso-multi-office-dental-it-infrastructure-guide

Maximizing Efficiency: Best Practices for Implementing Dental IT Solutions
In today’s fast-paced dental industry, staying ahead of the curve requires more than just exceptional patient care. It’s about leveraging technology to streamline operations, enhance patient experiences, and ultimately, grow your practice. In this blog, we’ll explore the best practices for implementing dental IT solutions that not only meet your practice’s needs but also set you apart in the competitive landscape.
Read the full article here: https://www.darkhorsetech.com/blogs/maximizing-efficiency-best-practices-for-implementing-dental-it-solutions

The ROI of Dental IT: How Technology Investments Boost Your Practice's Bottom Line
In the ever-evolving world of dentistry, staying ahead of the curve is more crucial than ever. Investing in the right technology can mean the difference between a thriving practice and one that's merely surviving. Dental IT solutions not only streamline operations but also significantly enhance patient care, leading to increased satisfaction and loyalty. But how exactly do these technological advancements translate into a tangible return on investment (ROI) for your practice? In this blog, we'll explore the multifaceted benefits of dental IT and how they can substantially boost your bottom line.
Read the full article here: https://www.darkhorsetech.com/blogs/the-roi-of-dental-it-how-technology-investments-boost-your-practices-bottom-line

November 1st, 2025

We hope this message finds you well! To continue providing industry-leading cybersecurity, HIPAA compliance, and IT support, Darkhorse Tech will be making a modest pricing adjustment. As cyberattacks targeting the dental industry grow more sophisticated, we’re investing heavily in advanced defenses — including annual independent cybersecurity audits — to ensure your practice stays secure and compliant.
 
As we enter our 13th year serving dental professionals, we remain committed to minimizing price increases while maintaining the high-quality service you expect. This adjustment reflects rising staffing and vendor costs, as well as inflation, ensuring we can continue investing in the people and technology that keep your practice protected and productive.
 
Effective January 1, 2026, Darkhorse Tech’s prices will increase by 3.9%. This modest adjustment balances today’s economic realities with our commitment to fair pricing. It remains below the vendor cost increases many practices are seeing and allows us to reward and retain top talent while continuing to deliver the specialized, dental-specific IT solutions your team relies on.
 
We are deeply grateful for your continued trust and partnership. Every dollar we reinvest goes toward enhancing our ability to protect your data, strengthen your cybersecurity posture, and make your technology experience seamless — so you can focus fully on providing excellent patient care.
 
Thank you for your continued support. We look forward to serving you in the coming year and beyond.
 
Warm regards,

Reuben Kamp
CEO, Darkhorse Tech

campaigns.subject: Healthcare Data Updates for FL and WI
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Special Requirements in Florida & Wisconsin for Healthcare Data Offshoring & Storage

As healthcare practices explore or continue using cloud solutions, offshore vendors, and third‑party IT providers, it’s critical to understand that not all rules are federal. States like Florida and Wisconsin have passed their own laws/regulations that impose additional restrictions around patient data – especially when that data is stored or accessed outside the U.S. Knowing these state rules can protect your practice from unexpected compliance risk, fines, or even loss of licensure.

Below is what dental practices (and other provider types) need to know about Florida and Wisconsin’s special requirements, and what actions to take to ensure compliance.

Florida: SB 264 & the Ban on Offshore Storage of Health Records

Key Points:

  • Effective July 1, 2023, Florida Senate Bill 264 (CS/CS/SB 264, Chapter 2023‑33) amended the Florida Electronic Health Records Exchange Act. One of its major changes is a ban on offshore storage of certain patient health information for providers using certified electronic health record technology (CEHRT). (Mintz)
  • Under the law, all patient information stored in an off‑site physical or virtual environment — including third‑party or subcontracted cloud/IT vendors — must have data centers physically located in the continental U.S., U.S. territories, or Canada. (Leech Tishman: Legal Services)
  • It’s not just about where data is stored. The law also requires providers subject to it to attest (under penalty of perjury) upon initial licensure and upon renewal that they are compliant with the offshoring restriction. Non‑compliance can lead to disciplinary action by Florida’s regulatory bodies. (Mintz)
  • Another layer: the law also addresses who controls or has interests in vendors or entities that handle patient data. For example, it has restrictions related to “controlling interest” in entities with business relationships in certain “foreign countries of concern.” (Mintz)

Who It Applies To:

  • Providers using CEHRT — this includes many hospitals, clinics, dentists, etc., depending on whether they use technology certified under federal standards. (Bradley)
  • Third‑party vendors, subcontractors, and cloud providers who manage or store patient health data for Florida‑licensed providers. Those business relationships must comply with the storage location requirement. (Leech Tishman: Legal Services)

Implications for Dental Practices:

  • If your practice is in Florida or services Florida patients, make sure your PMS / EHR vendor is compliant. If data is stored in data centers abroad (outside U.S., territories, Canada), that may violate this law.
  • Contracts with vendors/business associates should include clauses verifying data storage locations, ownership interest disclosures, and attestations of compliance.
  • Licensure renewals or initial licensing in Florida will often require affirmation that you are compliant. So in practice, non‑compliance isn’t just a risk of fine — it may jeopardize your ability to obtain or renew your license.
  • Audits may be required, either internally or by state regulators; you may have to move data if it’s stored offshore.

Wisconsin: What the State Requires & What It Doesn’t

Key Points:

  • Wisconsin, like many states, requires providers to comply with HIPAA, but also imposes its own state laws governing confidentiality, health care records, and limitations on disclosure and release of patient health information. (Wisconsin Department of Health Services)
  • The Wisconsin Department of Health Services has materials (Health IT, Privacy & Security, etc.) that emphasize that providers must protect the privacy and security of ePHI, use disclosure rules, implement proper controls, follow state law regarding release of records, and support secure exchange of health information. (Wisconsin Department of Health Services)

Offshoring / Data Location in Wisconsin:

  • From currently available public sources, Wisconsin does not appear to have a law that explicitly bans offshoring of health data at the level of Florida’s SB 264. I didn’t find a statute similar to Florida requiring all patient records stored in cloud or third‑party facilities to be maintained inside U.S./Canada territories. (But this may change — always good to monitor.)
  • However, Wisconsin does have its “release” and “use” laws; providers must follow state rules on when PHI can be shared, who it's shared with, and under what conditions. If data is stored offshore, that may complicate compliance, especially with regard to disclosures, retention, and lawful access. Wisconsin’s laws also impose strict controls on medical records’ confidentiality (for example, who can request release and under what authorization) and require providers to follow both state and federal law. (DATCP)

Implications for Dental Practices:

  • Even if Wisconsin doesn’t currently ban offshoring in all cases, using offshore storage or off‑shore vendors increases complexity and risk — from vendor management, contract review, ensuring training, and ensuring legal jurisdiction.
  • You should ensure your vendor agreements / business associate agreements reflect clear provisions about location of data storage, data security, breach notifications, and access rights.
  • When dealing with patient consent, disclosures, and state requirements for records release, having data stored offshore may make meeting Wisconsin law more challenging (e.g., timely response, jurisdictional issues).

Best Practices for Compliance in Florida & Wisconsin

Given the state‑level requirements, here are steps dental practices and providers should take to minimize legal risk and maintain data privacy:

  1. Audit where every piece of patient data is stored. Not just your internal systems—what about your cloud vendors, backups, subcontractors, or IT partners?
  2. Review vendor contracts / BAAs to ensure they explicitly state storage location restrictions (especially if operating in Florida), include security and encryption obligations, and provide for state law compliance.
  3. Verify that your EHR or PMS is “certified” if applicable (especially in Florida) and that you understand whether CEHRT is required under your provider status.
  4. Attest or certify as required by state law — for example, in Florida, make sure all licensure/renewal paperwork is up to date and includes the required affidavits of compliance.
  5. Have a plan for data migration if necessary. If you discover your vendor stores data offshore and that’s a problem under state law, you’ll need to move that data to compliant facilities and ensure transition in contracts.
  6. Ensure breach notification and incident response processes cover offshore or out‑of‑state storage situations. Contracts should define breach responsibility, reporting time frames, etc.
  7. Monitor regulatory changes. These laws evolve; what is true today may change. Providers must stay aware of new state laws, amendments, or guidance.

Why This Matters: Risks & Costs

  • Licensure risk: Non‑compliance in Florida can threaten professional licensure or lead to disciplinary actions.
  • Legal and financial exposure: Breaches or violations can lead to fines, civil liability, contractual penalties.
  • Patient trust & reputation: If patient records are stored offshore against state law (or in vendors that do not comply), the reputational damage can be significant.
  • Operational burden: Audits, data migrations, contract renegotiations — all require time and resources. But much more costly if unplanned under pressure.

How Darkhorse Tech Can Help

At Darkhorse Tech, we specialize in helping dental practices ensure compliance with both federal HIPAA requirements and applicable state laws like Florida’s SB 264 and state privacy rules in Wisconsin. Here’s how we assist:

  • Vendor audits & contract reviews to surface hidden offshore risks
  • Data location mapping and migration support to compliant storage regions
  • Ensuring your PMS / EHR solutions are certified (when required) and configured to meet state law obligations
  • Assisting with licensure compliance documentation, including attestations in Florida
  • Continuous monitoring & risk assessments so you are aware of emerging laws or changes

Conclusion

State‑level laws like Florida’s offshoring ban and stricter storage location requirements are no longer outliers — they’re part of a fast‑evolving landscape. For practices in Florida, compliance with SB 264 is mandatory if you use or operate with certified electronic health record technology. For practices in Wisconsin (and many other states), the risk may be less overt today, but cumulative legal, contractual, and reputational pressures make ignoring offshore storage a dangerous bet.

If your practice is using cloud PMS, EHR, or outsourcing data services, it’s time to get proactive. Don’t wait for an audit or a regulatory issue to force you to scramble. Reach out to ensure your systems, contracts, and data practices are fully compliant — wherever your data may be stored.

Hello!

We hope you're doing well! Just wanted to gently remind you (one final time - I promise these emails will stop!) about an important upcoming change:

Windows 10 will reach the end of its official support in October 2025.

This means your PCs will continue to function, but they'll stop receiving critical security updates required to keep your systems compliant and secure. To make sure you're well-prepared and protected, here are your options:

  • Upgrade to Windows 11: Most newer computers can handle this upgrade, but it typically requires a new Windows 11 license.
  • Check Eligibility: Not sure if your current computers qualify for the upgrade? No worries—let us know, and we'll quickly confirm for you.
  • Replace Older Computers: Unfortunately, older hardware can't support Windows 11 effectively, or it might slow down significantly. Replacement will be necessary in these cases.


Important Note: Cyber liability insurance will typically deny claims if non-compliant operating systems are in use, so staying updated is crucial.

We know October 2025 is almost here, so please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions or concerns—we're always here to help.

Warm regards,

Hello!

We hope you're doing well! Just wanted to gently remind you (for the 4th time—sorry, we promise we're just looking out for you!) about an important upcoming change:

Windows 10 will reach the end of its official support in October 2025.

This means your PCs will continue to function, but they'll stop receiving critical security updates required to keep your systems compliant and secure. To make sure you're well-prepared and protected, here are your options:

  • Upgrade to Windows 11: Most newer computers can handle this upgrade, but it typically requires a new Windows 11 license.
  • Check Eligibility: Not sure if your current computers qualify for the upgrade? No worries—let us know, and we'll quickly confirm for you.
  • Replace Older Computers: Unfortunately, older hardware can't support Windows 11 effectively, or it might slow down significantly. Replacement will be necessary in these cases.


Important Note: Cyber liability insurance will typically deny claims if non-compliant operating systems are in use, so staying updated is crucial.

We know October 2025 feels far away, but being proactive now can save you headaches later! Please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions or concerns—we're always here to help.

Warm regards,

Your Friends at Darkhorse Tech

HIPAA Security Rule Updates: What Dental Practices Need to Know
As the CEO of Darkhorse Tech, I want to bring to your attention some significant proposed changes to the HIPAA Security Rule that could have a direct impact on your dental practice. On December 27, 2024, the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to update the Security Rule for the first time in over a decade. The official version was published on January 6, 2025. These updates are designed to improve clarity, enhance cybersecurity measures, and ensure better compliance in protecting electronic protected health information (ePHI). Let's break down what this means for dental practices.
Read full article here: https://www.darkhorsetech.com/blogs/hipaa-security-rule-updates-what-dental-practices-need-to-know

Hello!  

We wanted to bring to your attention the fact that Windows 10 will reach its end of support in October of 2025. While your PC will still function, it will no longer receive the necessary security updates to maintain compliance. With this being said, we wanted to alert you to this pending change, and provide you with some options to ensure you are protected.

  • Newer computers can be upgraded to Windows 11
  • This does require a new Windows 11 license in most cases
  • If you are unsure if your computers are eligible to be upgraded, please let us know and we can confirm.
  • Older computers will need to be replaced. Windows 11 won’t run on older hardware, or will see significant performance issues.
**Cyber liability insurance will deny any claims if there are non-compliant operating systems.**

Remember that staying on an unsupported operating system poses security risks, so we encourage you to take action before the end of support date.   While this is still months from now, we wanted to proactively get in touch so we can address any questions or concerns you may have.  

Regards,

Safeguarding Patient Data: Understanding Cloud Hosted Systems in Dental Offices
Darkhorse Dental IT Education
In an era where digitalization permeates every aspect of our lives, the healthcare sector, including dental offices, faces an increasing need to protect sensitive patient data. Cloud hosted data emerges as a pivotal solution in this endeavor, offering secure, scalable, and accessible platforms for data management. In the context of dental practices, understanding the nuances of cloud hosted data is important not only for safeguarding patient information but also for ensuring compliance with stringent and sometimes expensive regulatory frameworks like the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
 
IT Myths and Misconceptions in Cybersecurity and HIPAA Compliance for Dental Offices
Open Dental Blog
In today’s wild-west of a digital age, dental offices must navigate the complex landscape of cybersecurity and HIPAA compliance. However, misconceptions and myths often cloud the judgment of dental professionals, leading to vulnerabilities and compliance issues. With this in mind, let’s debunk some common myths and offer practical tips to help dental offices maintain robust cybersecurity and ensure HIPAA compliance.

Almost Three-quarters of Ransomware Victims Hit Multiple Times
The HIPAA Journal
A recent study conducted by the cybersecurity firm Semperis has revealed that companies are often targeted by ransomware groups multiple times, with almost three-quarters (74%) of companies that experienced a ransomware attack saying they had been attacked multiple times. These attacks caused disruption at 87% of attacked companies, 37% reported suffering data loss and 33% of companies said they had to take all of their systems offline. In healthcare, 40% suffered data loss and 29% had to take all of their systems offline.

campaigns.name: Windows 10 Reminder
campaigns.subject: Windows 10 End of Life 2025 - Will You Be Ready?
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser

Hello!  

We wanted to bring to your attention the fact that Windows 10 will reach its end of support in October of 2025. While your PC will still function, it will no longer receive the necessary security updates to maintain compliance. With this being said, we wanted to alert you to this pending change, and provide you with some options to ensure you are protected.

  • Newer computers can be upgraded to Windows 11
  • This does require a new Windows 11 license in most cases
  • If you are unsure if your computers are eligible to be upgraded, please let us know and we can confirm.
  • Older computers will need to be replaced. Windows 11 won’t run on older hardware, or will see significant performance issues.

Remember that staying on an unsupported operating system poses security risks, so we encourage you to take action before the end of support date.   While this is still over a year from now, we wanted to proactively get in touch so we can address any questions or concerns you may have.  

Regards,
Darkhorse Tech

This presentation training is for Darkhorse clients only! Join Darkhorse CEO & Founder, Reuben Kamp, alongside Matt DiBlasi, CEO of Abyde, to better understand current cybersecurity attacks in the healthcare space and what you can do to prevent them. Password: Darkhorse2324!
 
 
News
 
Top News: The Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (HITECH) Act of 2009 requires the HHS’ Office for Civil Rights to conduct periodic audits of HIPAA-regulated entities to assess compliance with the HIPAA Rules. OCR Director Melanie Fontes Rainer has confirmed that audits will be taking place this year and will focus on HIPAA Security Rule compliance.
 
Data Security
 
FBI Warns of Credible Cybersecurity Threat to Dental Practices
American Dental Association News
The American Dental Association (ADA) urges all dental practices to remain vigilant after it was contacted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) with information regarding a credible threat to the practices of oral and maxillofacial surgeons.
 
The Perils of Enlisting Friends and Family IT Support For Your Dental Practice
Darkhorse Dental IT Education
In an era where cyberattacks lurk around every corner and are evolving by the day and even by the hour, many businesses, especially smaller ones, often rely on the tech-savvy skills of family members to manage their IT needs. 
 
Vital Role of Cybersecurity in Dental Practices
Darkhorse Dental IT Education
Dental practices, like many small businesses, may not perceive themselves as prime targets for cyberattacks. However, the reality is quite the opposite. The sensitive nature of patient data, including personal and financial information, makes dental offices attractive targets for cybercriminals. 
 
New Jersey Dermatology Practice Suffers 380,000-Record Data Break
HIPAA Journal
Morristown, NJ-based Affiliated Dermatologists and Dermatologic Surgeons (ADDS) has announced a major breach of patient data. On March 5, 2024, ADDS found a ransom note on its network that claimed its network had been breached and data had been stolen. 
 
Black Basta Ransomware Group Targeting Healthcare Organizations
HIPAA Journal
All healthcare and public health (HPH) sector organizations have been warned to be on high alert and to implement mitigations against Black Basta ransomware attacks, as the ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group has the HPH sector in its crosshairs.
 
Cybersecurity in Dentistry: Safeguarding Patient Information in the Digital Age
Dentistry Today
From electronic health records (EHRs) to digital imaging and cloud-based appointment scheduling, the digitization of dentistry has brought about unprecedented efficiency and patient care improvements. However, this shift also introduces a critical challenge: the need for robust cybersecurity measures to protect sensitive patient data.
 
HIPAA
 
OCR HIPAA Audit Program to Commence in 2024
The HIPAA Journal
The high numbers of data breaches now being reported strongly suggest that many healthcare organizations are not fully compliant with the HIPAA Security Rule or that the safeguards they have implemented to comply with HIPAA are not proving to be effective. Another round of audits is necessary to establish the current state of compliance and will help OCR’s future efforts to improve cybersecurity across the healthcare sector.
 
37% of Healthcare Organizations Do Not Have a Security Incident Response Plan
The HIPAA Journal
A recent survey of IT professionals has revealed that 37% of healthcare organizations* do not have a security incident response plan in place, despite it being a requirement of HIPAA. 
 
The Truth Can Be Expensive: Why HIPAA Compliance is Non-Negotiable for Dental Offices
Darkhorse Dental IT Education
In the fast-paced world of dental care and constant news of cyberattacks, patient trust is vitally important. Yet, many dental offices unknowingly jeopardize this trust by overlooking a critical aspect of healthcare regulation: HIPAA compliance. The consequences of non-compliance can be severe, ranging from hefty fines to irreparable damage to reputation.

November 1st, 2023
 
 
Very exciting news! Some of you may have seen the announcement on social media that we have partnered with the leading Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) Cyber Security company. Huntress is their name, and they are the champions of the space.
 
What does this mean for your business? Starting on 11/1 you will see a SKU change on your invoice. Bitdefender is being replaced with Huntress. What this fully means is that you’re getting two products for the price of one. Bitdefender is Anti-Virus, and Huntress is Anti-Virus with EDR.
 
EDR solutions are a more advanced and modern form of protection. They monitor and record activities happening on endpoints (devices connected to a network, like computers and mobile devices), searching for suspicious patterns of behavior rather than specific signatures. This is a 24x7 human layer of protection.

When an EDR tool identifies potentially harmful behavior, it can either alert a human security analyst or take pre-configured actions like isolating the affected endpoint from the network. EDR tools can help identify and mitigate threats like zero-day attacks and APTs, which can evade traditional anti-virus solutions.

EDR solutions also offer visibility into the threat landscape and provide tools for investigating security incidents. They can create a timeline of events leading up to a detected threat, making it easier to understand the source of an attack, its progression, and its impact on the system or network.
In essence, it is Anti-Virus 2.0!
 
In addition, to help you educate your staff, Huntress and Darkhorse would like to offer you free access to two relevant episodes of our Security Awareness Training:

• Password Managers - to help explain why these tools are so important to keeping organizations safe
• Passwords - to teach users about risks of weak passwords and how to come up with a strong 16-character password.
 
We are making them available in a free, zero-configuration way throughout the month of October. You and your staff can simply go to mycurricula.com and enter the code 95SSPp$k#TaT along with any email address. Our hope is that this will help you drive best password security practices across your employees.
 
--
 
The second part of this announcement is to remind you of the minimal annual change to the price of your Darkhorse Tech HIPAA Compliance, Cybersecurity and Support Services subscriptions.
 
Darkhorse is in year eleven and we have worked hard to keep price increases to a minimum. This decision was made carefully analyzing market conditions, costs of good, and increased staffing and living expenses.
 
Starting Jan 1st, 2024, Darkhorse prices will adjust by 3% to ensure the innovation you expect from Darkhorse continues to benefit you and your patients.

campaigns.name: UPDATE: Aspen Dental Cybersecurity Breach - Situational Report and Resources
campaigns.subject: UPDATE: Aspen Dental Cybersecurity Breach - Situational Report and Resources
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Good Morning, and thank you for being great partners of Darkhorse Tech. We have been getting many emails regarding the Aspen situation and we wanted to get some information regarding this, how Darkhorse protects your practice and explain how Aspen is set up (differently).

Aspen’s Database Structure: Aspen’s system is set up uniquely. They are not cloud, in fact they host all of their servers in house, with their own proprietary PMS software. When they got hit, it hit all their offices because everything is centralized. This is the first big takeaway of our systems vs theirs. All our client’s data is not connected in any way, this is both a cybersecurity as well as HIPAA compliance standard.
 
Backup Systems: Let’s start with defining a term called Air Gapped Backups: “This backup is a type of data backup that is stored physically separate from the primary system or network. This separation ensures that the backup remains secure and inaccessible to potential cyber-attacks, malware, or unauthorized access. By keeping the backup isolated, it provides an extra layer of protection to help recover critical data in the event of system failure or security breaches.”
We now know they did not have air-gapped backups simply because they have been down since April 25th.  Clean backups would have had them up by now. 

Takeaway - you are doing everything you need to (and us) to meet your HIPAA compliance requirements from the IT/technical standpoint.

Last year, we did email everybody and let them know we highly recommend adding the Blackpoint Cyber and Abyde HIPAA Compliance Management as another layer to all practices.

Blackpoint Cyber MDR (Managed Detection and Response): Blackpoint Cyber is a cybersecurity company that specializes in providing advanced threat detection, response, and remediation solutions to help protect businesses and organizations against cyber-attacks. Their services typically include Managed Detection and Response (MDR), risk assessments, and cyber consulting. By leveraging cutting-edge technology and expert security personnel, Blackpoint Cyber aims to help clients secure their networks, safeguard sensitive data, and maintain compliance with industry standards and regulations.
  • https://blackpointcyber.com/
  • It’s a 24x7x365 Human Layer Service
  • Theory behind this is hackers want to get into the system when business is closed, on holiday ETC.
  • This protects and detects odd and bad user behavior on the network and stops it there. Currently this is not addressed by Firewall or AntiVirus and this is where it comes in.
  • It is $14/agent/month for the service, however since the Aspen event they are running a promotion this month for $12.
Abyde HIPAA Compliance, Stress Free Compliance Software: Abyde is a company that provides HIPAA compliance software and solutions to healthcare providers, particularly targeting small and medium-sized practices. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) is a US law that establishes requirements for the protection of sensitive patient information. Abyde's software and services are designed to simplify the process of achieving and maintaining HIPAA compliance by offering risk assessments, guided training, policy and procedure templates, and ongoing support to help healthcare providers navigate the complex regulations and safeguard patient data.
  • https://abyde.com/darkhorse-tech/
  • The main rep for this company is Chris Wheaton cwheaton@abyde.com, who is very responsive and has been a great partner to many mutual clients.
Let me know if you have any more questions on this, and rest assured, we will continue to monitor this situation.
 
Regards,
 
Reuben Kamp
CEO
Darkhorse Tech

campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Good Morning,

Sometimes I need a nudge to complete a task that only benefits me, I’m weird like that.  Last week while walking my dog I felt a new sensation I hadn’t had before… exciting!  There was a raw, almost itchy feeling on my big toe.  As I sat down on the stone wall in front of the park in my neighborhood my dog gave me a quizzical look.  What I found at the bottom of my shoe was a gaping hole and as I waggled my big toe in time with my pups tail it was as if some shoe creature was waving at me from it’s home.

A few weeks prior I had considered replacing my running shoes, my feet were getting sore after exercise and that felt premature for my age.  That said, my kids are headed back to school soon so I prioritized outfits and footwear that would make them feel excited to walk through the doors on their first day.  Once they were set the idea of new shoes sort of left my mind even after multiple days in a row ending with an aching for an ice bath.

If you’ve made it this far it’s about to pay off.  My shoes arrived, it’s almost like having something in my life I had never had before, something that immediately made a difference and resulted in me having more energy at night, more ability to complete house projects. 

Dental-specific IT is a lot like a new pair of shoes, you may not prioritize it but once you’ve experienced the difference it’s hard to imagine you survived without it.  I’d love for my team to have the opportunity to speak with you about your IT pain points and offer solutions that might really help you get back to focusing on growing your business and pleasing your patients.  If you are ready to do something for yourself, please reach out to us.

campaigns.subject: Keyboard Tough Guy
campaigns.html:
View this email in your browser
Hello,

When I was a kid tough guy movies were a pretty big deal.  Less for me because I was the kid on the soccer field picking clover buds as the ball whizzed by my head but my good friends and protectors loved an action movie centered around a really, tough, guy.  I knew this because I would watch R rated movies at my friend’s houses (I wasn’t allowed).  Without fail, at some point the main character would get mad about something and punch a wall, wow, that was tough.  Since we were inept at dealing with our emotions, this seemed like a perfectly reasonable way to express ourselves, and look really cool.  To this day our childhood homes carry the scars of stupidity and our hands will never be the same.

As computer jobs replaced Rambo jobs it was as if the basement door was replaced by a keyboard and movies started depicting scene after scene of someone smashing their keyboard in anger.  In a world of desk-bound humans, this is the new tough guy calling card.  While not a door, smashing a keyboard can still inflict pain, it also doesn’t fix anything (emotionally or on a computer), you need a level head and some troubleshooting for that.

Please visit our blog to learn more about ways to troubleshoot your own computer and if all else fails how to prep for a service call.  After all, you probably only have so many keyboards laying around.  If you’d like to talk 80’s movies or something Dental-IT related, please reach out to us.

Hello,

You can do a lot of things on your own, this past week I was contemplating learning a new skill or paying a professional.  As a fan of DIY (I like tinkering!) I decided that the insides of a dryer shouldn't be a complete mystery to me so when ours was no longer making things dry, just dizzy, it seemed like a good time to do some research.

After a lot of YouTubing and some research on Samsung dryers I decided I could handle the job.  I ordered what I assumed was the right part, disassembled the dryer, kept the screws well organized  removed and replaced what I believed the be the malfunctioning component and reverse engineered the dryer.  VUALA!  Our dryer was still a clothes-dizzying machine.

After some more research I decided it was another piece I needed so, that is on order.  That said, a well timed blog post made me wonder if I had also destroyed our dryer for good.  While clothes drying is not the same as running a dental practice through a server, what I learned while putting together our latest blog really had me pondering the intelligence of my choice.

Hello,

With the new HIPAA regulations we sent you an email regarding our recommendation when it comes to HIPAA compliance software - Abyde.  Many of you reached out asking what else you could do to protect your practice, not only from cyber threats but from falling afoul of the law.  At the time we were doing our due diligence and have since found a solution we feel great about – Blackpoint Cyber, a Security Operations Center.
 
A Security Operations Center: cyber security professionals constantly monitoring your network as well as the greater cyber threat activity at large.  With real-time threat detection, 24/7 active monitoring and response, and the ability to deploy agents in real time a Security Operations Center takes you from reactive to proactive and beyond.
 
What Does a Security Operations Center Do?
 
  • Proactive Monitoring:  A key element of a Security Operations Center is the proactive nature of their work.  Whether focusing on PCs, Servers, Routers, Firewalls, or even Mobile Devices, a security operation center is constantly reviewing a network for vulnerabilities by looking at it from an “criminal” perspective.  On top of this oversight the monitoring aspect considers cyber threats in general (not necessarily within a given network) to prevent attacks from being successful should they take place.  Last, monitoring means identifying malicious activity before it can become an issue.
  • Incident Response & Recovery:  While malicious activity can often be addressed before it becomes an issue, should an incident occur a Security Operations Center allows an organization to continue operating while remediation takes place. 
  • Remediation Activities: A majority of remediation revolves around making adjustments to a setup in order to prevent future attacks and incidents.  With their specialization they are able to identify vulnerabilities and respond accordingly.
  • Compliance:  As specialists a Security Operations Center can ensure that security standards are upheld in accordance with best practice and industry specific guidelines.

Blackpoint Cyber MDR (Managed Detection and Response) has proven to be an invaluable addition to a Dentist’s security stack.  Blackpoint Cyber is a proactive, offensive approach to keep you ahead of cyber criminals.  They utilize continuous monitoring, real-time threat detection and active response to protect Dental practices.
 
An added bonus is Blackpoint Cyber’s cost structure, a deal when you consider you are getting an actual, human-based team of technicians, not an automated (or outsourced) “team”.  What do we mean by affordable?  Blackpoint Cyber offers a free demo, 10 day proof of concept, followed by a call with a Blackpoint Engineer and member of Darkhorse Tech to run through findings and answer any questions you may have.  The cost, should you choose to move forward is $14 dollars per endpoint (computer, server, etc.) making their offer a true value.  To schedule your demo please reach out to us and mention Blackpoint in the space provided.

Good Morning,

It has been a while since we reached out to our clients to check in and request feedback. Based on some changes over the last year we were hoping to elicit your help.  As you may be aware we took some time over Covid to review our service delivery, based on client feedback we focused on implementing a system that would better allocate our resources to our client’s needs. 

What does that mean exactly?  We have three tiers of technicians, level 1,2, and 3.  Technicians in level 1 focus on daily concerns, level 2 focus on slightly more complex tickets which may take longer to resolve and level 3 technicians focus on issues that require a “project” mindset or those which, may impact your ability to function as a business.  The goal of Agile service is to prioritize your ticket handling in the most quick and efficient way possible with the appropriate asset focused on the issue at hand.

While it took some time to implement (and certainly came with a few growing pains) this change has proven to be most beneficial to our clients.  Ticket response times are down significantly and the feedback since full implementation has been overwhelmingly positive.

That said, I am asking for constructive feedback based on the last few months of service.  What is going well, what do you have questions about, and do you have any lingering frustrations?  Please feel free to reach out to me directly at brian@darkhorsetech.com

Hello,

It’s easy to forget a near constant in our lives, something we see more of during a week than most friends and even partners.  Through the good, the bad, the ugly and everything in between our workplace is there, it accepts us no matter what; we eat, drink, socialize, laugh, and cry where we work so why is it so rare to revere the space that treats us so well?

Working from home makes this a little easier as “home” connotates love, warmth, comfort.  You want your home to feel lived in but not look like it’s been lived through.  With that idea in mind and wanting to give back to the space that has treated me so well for the last 2.5 years of work-from-home status I decided to have a painter out to provide an estimate.

As we discussed the staining of the shingles vs the painting of the siding, I mentioned that I’d love for him to provide two estimates, one for the whole house, one for just the second level as I planned to paint the lower half myself.  He looked at me and I immediately saw myself in his unblinking eyes… even if I did do the work myself why would I treat something that has been so good to me with anything other than a professional makeover?

Sure, if I wanted to paint the house myself I could and in the process I would probably learn a lot about painting but the mistakes might be costly or worse, compromise the longevity of the façade.  With the love of my home in mind I stopped myself mid-sentence and requested a single quote. If you're ready to trust your business to a team of IT professionals who will care for it as you do, please reach out to us.

campaigns.preview: The best way to reach us and get quickest ticket response times.
campaigns.html:
The best way to reach us and get quickest ticket response times.
View this email in your browser
Hello!
 
As we continue our quest of strengthening our client relationships, one of the biggest topics we would like to review is the variety of ways to reach us. “But why would I need to know that, don’t I just call?” – Not if you want the most efficient and effective response.
 
Yes we have an 800 number but our team is large and only a few of us are operating the phones at a time whereas, our entire team is ready to pick up tickets when they are submitted.  So, what are the other ways of submitting a ticket and the benefits associated with them?  We’re glad you asked…
 
  • Submit a support ticket through our Customer Portal
    • This is the same portal that can be used for paying your bill, etc.
    • You can view all tickets you’ve submitted, the status of each ticket, all updates on your tickets, submit new tickets and even communicate directly with our team.
    • With so many options this is one of the most comprehensive options available to you
  • Email our Support team at support@darkhorsetech.com
    • This automatically creates a ticket on our Help Desk board
    • Making sure the Summary of your email is as descriptive as possible greatly helps us out, as we can immediately determine if there is a major problem (i.e., We Cannot Connect to Our Server) and our team can be allocated accordingly
    • Any of our team members can check the ticket, review the issue, and start resolving it
  • Submit a ticket via the Darkhorse icon on your desktop
    • If you hadn’t already noticed, there should be a small Darkhorse icon on the bottom right-hand corner of your desktop, tucked in next to the date and time
    • From here, right-click on the icon and Submit a ticket, sending it directly to our Help Desk board
    • Submitting a ticket this way is very easy since you don’t need to pick up the phone or use an email platform to submit
    • This also tags the computer name that you are submitting it from, making it easy for our team to know where the issue is occurring
  • Call us
    • This is always an option, and we have Service Coordinators who do their best to answer any call that comes in
    • Our phone system can get bogged down at some of the busier times of day, meaning that the Service Coordinators are not available as they are on other calls
    • If you do call, and aren’t able to get ahold of someone, please leave us a message! Our team will be listening to the messages quickly (as we receive email notifications with our VOIP phones) and updating accordingly
    • One thing to note here, is we do ask you to please not call in repeatedly, as that only makes our ability to respond to the calls that much more challenging.
  For a high resolution PDF of the best ways to contact us, click here!

We always value feedback, so please let us know if you have any questions!
 
Regards,

campaigns.subject: Process Update - Faster Response
campaigns.preview: The best way to reach us and get quickest ticket response times.
campaigns.html:
The best way to reach us and get quickest ticket response times.
View this email in your browser
Hello!
 
As we continue our quest of strengthening our client relationships, one of the biggest topics we would like to review is the variety of ways to reach us. “But why would I need to know that, don’t I just call?” – Not if you want the most efficient and effective response.
 
Yes we have an 800 number but our team is large and only a few of us are operating the phones at a time whereas, our entire team is ready to pick up tickets when they are submitted.  So, what are the other ways of submitting a ticket and the benefits associated with them?  We’re glad you asked…
 
  • Submit a support ticket through our Customer Portal
    • This is the same portal that can be used for paying your bill, etc.
    • You can view all tickets you’ve submitted, the status of each ticket, all updates on your tickets, submit new tickets and even communicate directly with our team.
    • With so many options this is one of the most comprehensive options available to you
  • Email our Support team at support@darkhorsetech.com
    • This automatically creates a ticket on our Help Desk board
    • Making sure the Summary of your email is as descriptive as possible greatly helps us out, as we can immediately determine if there is a major problem (i.e., We Cannot Connect to Our Server) and our team can be allocated accordingly
    • Any of our team members can check the ticket, review the issue, and start resolving it
  • Submit a ticket via the Darkhorse icon on your desktop
    • If you hadn’t already noticed, there should be a small Darkhorse icon on the bottom right-hand corner of your desktop, tucked in next to the date and time
    • From here, right-click on the icon and Submit a ticket, sending it directly to our Help Desk board
    • Submitting a ticket this way is very easy since you don’t need to pick up the phone or use an email platform to submit
    • This also tags the computer name that you are submitting it from, making it easy for our team to know where the issue is occurring
  • Call us
    • This is always an option, and we have Service Coordinators who do their best to answer any call that comes in
    • Our phone system can get bogged down at some of the busier times of day, meaning that the Service Coordinators are not available as they are on other calls
    • If you do call, and aren’t able to get ahold of someone, please leave us a message! Our team will be listening to the messages quickly (as we receive email notifications with our VOIP phones) and updating accordingly
    • One thing to note here, is we do ask you to please not call in repeatedly, as that only makes our ability to respond to the calls that much more challenging.
  For a high resolution PDF of the best ways to contact us, click here!

We always value feedback, so please let us know if you have any questions!
 
Regards,

Brian Ash

Hello Darkhorse Family!
 
We here at Darkhorse value all of our clients, and want to better understand what we’re doing well, and maybe not so well, for each of you. You can help us improve our services and we would greatly appreciate it.
 
Every time we work a ticket, and that ticket is completed, you will receive an automated email with a link to our survey. The reason we bring this up is that we want EVERYONE to respond to those as often as possible. Our goal is to get a more thorough understanding of your experience here, so we can better support you in this business relationship.

campaigns.preview: How is 2022 going so far?
campaigns.html:
How is 2022 going so far?
View this email in your browser
Hello,

A few years ago, I really wanted to follow through on the annual tradition of making plans to better myself in a variety of ways.  By the third week of the new year, I had yet to pick up a novel… or a guitar, exercise routine, extra hours of sleep or eight glasses of water a day (let alone three).  As I had tied all these goals to a calendar that would culminate in success at the end of the year, I had failed before I even began.

The third week of the new year will really test your mettle when it comes to resolutions - I hope your year is off to a strong start!  This week our team met for two full days to review the year that was and plan for the year that will be.  If I (me from a few years ago) were heading into this meeting I would have been hesitant to get my hopes up after all, the best laid plans have a way about them. 

Aside from the EOS system we implemented a few years ago this meeting had one key difference, I wasn’t alone, and I will be accountable to my team and them to me.  We weren’t just making plans of what we want to accomplish we made plans on how we can support each other to make sure we succeed.

Greatness can be accomplished alone but it is a whole heck of a lot easier when you have support.  If you are finding that IT is getting in the way of you accomplishing your goals, we would love to talk about how we might be a good fit to take some items off your plate - please reach back out to us.
Regards,

Important Notice

Hello,

We are writing this email, as we see that you originally purchased a Meraki MX67C firewall device, which includes a cellular failover option.  We realize that we should have followed up on the status of this during your original install and want to take a moment to apologize for that. We’re happy to jump on a call or answer any questions you may have about this.

We are contacting you today as we have noticed that the cellular failover in the device is still not set up, and that is something we can’t do without some help from you and your team. To clarify, this is not a required configuration, and it is up to you if you want to utilize it, but one that we want to be sure you are aware of in case you do want to have it enabled.

To properly configure the cellular failover, you will need to purchase a SIM card from a wireless retailer (Verizon, AT&T, etc.) and tie it to a service plan. Once you have the SIM card physically in the office, you would just need to let us know, and we can coordinate getting it configured in the Meraki.

If you have any questions about this, please let us know!

I love a good email, saying hello, making someone laugh, answering questions but recently I feel like the emails I have been sending to Dentists who have reached out to us in the past have been missing something.  Specifically, whether we might be the right fit for you and your business and vice versa.

When it comes to IT for your business there are a variety of ways to address your needs.  From covering IT yourself, handing it off to an employee or family member/friend, hiring a local IT person or (as you know from reaching out to us) engaging a Managed Service Provider.

There are pluses and minuses to all of these options and I probably need more space than this to get into it (you can find benefits of our model here ) but I would start the conversation with a question, does your current solution address all your needs currently?

campaigns.subject: How to Floss
campaigns.preview: You thought you knew but you have no idea.
campaigns.html:
You thought you knew but you have no idea.
View this email in your browser
Hello,
 
When I was learning how to floss my grandmother told me a story about a man-eating Dragon who never flossed.  A Knight’s sword found it’s way deep into the Dragon’s gums causing infection and eventually death.  Through gritted dentures my grandmother informed me that it was important to floss at least three times a day, to “snap” into the gum line (to remove any “swords”), to floss after brushing in case any of the bristles got stuck in my teeth and to not stop until I was bleeding.  I lived like that for years, with that lesson on flossing dictating my oral-care routine.  It wasn’t until I told my dentist about the dragon that he laughed me out of the chair and into some better oral hygiene habits.
 
Why did I take the advice of a relative who had no teeth and was trying to scare me into doing what she thought was right?
 
Why are you taking IT advice from your cousin (who loves computers), an individual or team that isn’t dental focused or anyone who is leveraging the fear of ransomware for their own gain? (There is a big difference between protecting against ransomware and selling through intimidation and it starts with education)
 
Dental IT is what we do in fact, it is ALL we do and not to sound too full of ourselves but we are really good at it (because we love it) and would love to help your practice free itself of any long-embedded “swords” -   please reach back out to us!

Increased Cybersecurity Threats and Protection Needed.
Just this year we’ve seen over 15 attacks, and many of them concentrated on dental, healthcare and key US infrastructure. They’ve taken out hundreds of dental offices, never to see their data again, hospitals and even gas pipelines. Keeping our clients secure is more important than it’s ever been. We’ve enhanced the internal security protection of our client’s practices even more this year and will continue to keep up to date on all the latest Cybersecurity standards. Enhancements to your Business and Your Support Team.
In the last 12 months we have invested in systems that address your #1 commodity – Time. Our team has spent the last 15 weeks training on the latest IT methodology called Agile. We have listened and worked tirelessly to meet aggressive response time goals, and we have 11 more support techs than we did this time last year. Reminders come in various forms, this one is animal shaped.

Hello,
 
I have these two holes in my yard, I noticed them about a month ago and thought to myself “I need to fill in those holes”. 
 
Three weeks ago, I was performing some yard maintenance (aimlessly wandering) and I twisted my ankle as my foot caught a sizable divot in the ground.  That was a crummy reminder, but I did think to myself “I really need to fill that in”. 
 
About two and a half weeks ago I was sipping a coffee on my porch when a movement out of the corner of my eye caught my attention, a Groundhog was staring at me… dead in the eyes.  Neither one of us moved for what felt like hours.  When it scampered off, I realized that those holes belonged to that Groundhog “that’s unfortunate” I thought as I remembered I needed to fill in those holes. 
 
To be honest, I haven’t done anything about the holes or the Groundhog but whenever I see that chubby little yard ornament, I think to myself “this is a way better reminder than twisting my ankle”. 
 
If your IT situation is the hole in your life, I really hope this email comes to you as more of a fuzzy creature and not an ankle-twisting lawn-blemish.  If you’d like to chat Dental-Specific IT or the perils of home ownership, please reach out to us.

Hello,
 
Heat cranking with the windows locked in the up position, music blasting from the questionable speakers, arguing over whether to stop and ask for directions… classic.  Cliché or not the struggle surrounding wayfinding advice from a “local” while on a family road trip was a real thing before smart phones. 
 
First, are you getting good directions or questionable? Do you trust someone just because they seem nice and like they know where they are?  Then there is the always confounding issue that you are in a hurry and without fail the advice giver can’t wait to provide a full century history of the place you find yourself, not just directions out of there.
 
Sure, sometimes you still hit a “no service” area but Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps, all do a great job of getting you where you need to go efficiently and effectively without the hemming and hawing with a dash of local face-melting lore.

campaigns.subject: What's the Stink-Bomb in Your Life?
campaigns.preview: As I stepped out of the hot, crowded, buzzing subway a smell hit me that I can not or maybe will not try to explain
campaigns.html:
As I stepped out of the hot, crowded, buzzing subway a smell hit me that I can not or maybe will not try to explain
View this email in your browser

Hello,  (want to talk to us and skip the story? - reach back out to us here!)
 
As I stepped out of the hot, crowded, buzzing subway a smell hit me that I can not or maybe will not try to explain .  All I can say is that my toes literally curled in my shoes, my chest caved in like I had just been punched and through watering eyes I reached out to try and catch my balance.  Day one of the start of my professional career in my new home (New York City) was off to an inauspicious start.  That said, it was my first job after University, I was just excited to be part of the hoard of people trying to make it there so they could eventually make it anywhere.
 
I made the same commute every day for a year before I took my first trip out of the city.  I was given the opportunity to visit another branch of our business and shadow someone in my role to see how we might learn from one another. So, I met the Yang to my Yin at his home and we hopped in his car, drove a couple of minutes (passing parks and a forest preserve along the way) to the office where we parked in the shade of a willow and went to work. That was the day that everything changed.
 
 I hadn’t given much thought to the cramped accommodations I had grown accustomed to or the fluctuations in temperature and smell above or below ground.  I had become numb or blissfully unaware to those things that were quietly taking a toll on me.  At 3pm, my typical meltdown-hour of the day I was still full of energy and cracking jokes with the team while working on our project.  I had become so used to the toll my commute was taking on me that I had stopped noticing how awful it was and I was blind to what it was doing to me.  It took a few weeks but eventually I got my transfer and said goodbye to the city forever.
 
Don’t let running your own IT or putting up with a sub-par solution become your daily commute or your subway stop stink-bomb.  Don’t get used to a situation that may be causing you more harm than you even realize.  Let us provide you with Dental Specific IT and get back to what really matters, your practice and your patients, say “no more” today and reach back out to us!
 
Regards,
Brian Ash
Chief Marketing Officer
