Hello,

It’s finals week, in fact, my last final is in one hour and I have just learned something dreadful, debilitating, gut-wrenching, soul-crushing… I forgot about Philosophy of the Twilight Zone, the one course I need to graduate.  Not only did I forget about the test, I forgot about the class, I havn’t been all year and now I have one hour to learn all there is to know about the Twilight Zone and it’s philosophy and my University career depends on it.
I know I’m stressed when I have this dream.  I have been out of college for close to two decades, I have no finals, just stress manifesting as obscure courses and their tests in my head.  Why do I stress?  Probably like everyone else I stress when I feel like I am missing something, like I don’t have everything under control, because I don’t.  Who does? 

We could all use a little help sometimes to free us up to focus on the things that really matter when it comes to our business.  Feeling behind is one thing, feeling behind because we don’t, won’t or aren’t sure where to ask for help is another altogether.  When I need help at work I have a team of motivated, talented and reliable people at my disposal.  When our clients need help they have those same individuals working together for their benefit only a click away.

When it comes to Dental IT, who do you have to turn to?  Can you rely on them to resolve your issues in an effective, efficient and timely manner?  When you consider IT for your practice does your head spin?  Our philosophy here at Darkhorse Tech is simple, pull our clients out of the Twilight Zone and free them up to focus on their practice and their patients.  If you need a little help, Please Reach out!

Hello,

I imagine the first person who walked by a Durian tree in the Malaysian wilderness didn’t think twice and just kept walking.  The tree itself is rather unremarkable aside from the spined fruit which seems to be a pretty solid deterrent.  The path of least resistance seems like a solid option.  That said if one were starving, desperate for food and the only thing around for miles was a Durian tree, well...

So, there they are, starving and staring at a spined pod which is nearly impossible to get open without spiking their hands and then it hits them, that corpse-like aroma the Durian is known for.  At this point they are aware there is fruit in there, it may be rotten and they may bleed-out getting to it but they have to try, they are starving after all. A few Durian-leaf bandages later they have managed to crack open the shell and the smell that was getting in the way before is now overwhelming.  No worry, plug the nose and take a bite… Heaven, or so I am told.

Now that I work from my home office I try to get out of the house after work.  I will go for a run or take the dog for a walk, anything to breathe some fresh air and refresh.  This Wednesday I didn’t move from my chair; my news feed was billowing smoke and I couldn’t pull myself away from the screen no matter how much I needed to.

I wanted a drink, something refreshing and bland, easy, calm, simple.  In the back of my fridge I found  a red white and blue can of beer, seemed tragic and fitting all at the same time… I deemed it appropriate and happy hour commenced.
Needing a break I decided to do a little research on this can of beer I was enjoying, turns out the company’s annual sales dropped from 18 million barrels in the late 70’s to less than a million by late 2001.  With the appointing of a new CEO those numbers have steadily increased and a turnaround for the ages was born.

Sometimes all you need is a fresh start.  Whether the excuse is a new year, winds of change, a poke from a friend, whatever - if you feel that itch you just have to scratch it.

Here at Darkhorse Tech we are all about providing a fresh start, please let us walk you through how we might be able to make your practice run smoother and give you peace of mind with our no-downtime solution and comprehensive threat protection, please schedule a call with me!

I love a good road-trip.  One that meanders through all sorts of back roads and avoids the highway and its billboards.  What is the fun in a billboard when back roads might unveil a hand-painted sign for something like “Wildlife Tour”?  Follow that hand-painted sign and you just might stumble across the owner of the tour extolling the virtues of keeping one’s guard up… extolling those virtues while holding up a hand with one, maybe two missing digits.

Last week I had to fire my plumber.

However, I didn’t just fire my wishy-washy, talkative, horrible house guest of a plumber, she is my cousin and now Thanksgiving is going to be really uncomfortable (and no, not because of the masks).
Having always felt like I put enough into my old house I figured it was important to save a little bit where I could, and the headache of dealing with unfinished projects not to mention mixing business with family was worth it in the end, at least until I met my new plumbers.

campaigns.name: Don't Forget Your Sunscreen
campaigns.subject: Don't Forget Your Sunscreen
campaigns.html:
Hello,

I spent a lot of time at the beach as a kid and with that time came pearls of wisdom from my grandparents, mostly unheeded.  “Make sure you don’t get your hands wet before you eat your sandwich.  Put on Sunscreen or you will regret it.  Don’t go swimming right after you eat, you might cramp up and have to be pulled out of the water by the lifeguard like what happened to your friend.”  I ate a lot of sand-sandwiches as a kid, I ate them by the light of my sun-radiated arms because a little burn and sand in my teeth would not stop me from swimming.  It was, however, rare for me to go sprinting into the ocean after eating because drowning would certainly put an end to a day at the beach.
As an IT Company the advice we give could fall into these two categories, preventing drowning and warning against sand-sandwiches and sunburns. Recently we were working with a partner who didn’t heed our advice from 2019 to replace their server.  The server crashed and they were facing data-loss, downtime, and lost revenue, or at least they would have been if they hadn’t implemented our backup and downtime solution.  Just a few minutes after losing their server, they were back up and running while we worked on getting them a replacement for the server they had lost.  In essence, they may have enjoyed a sand-sandwich and sunburn, but they were free to go for a swim.
 
Our partners aren’t going to listen to all of our advice, but they trust us to let them know when a situation is dire and requires a solution that will solve their immediate needs.  We are also always ready with suggestions that will help them grow and push forward safe, sound and ready to tackle whatever else comes their way as business owners and Dental Professionals.
 
If you are ready to learn more about how we can safeguard your practice and provide solutions for emergencies as well as every-day situations, please schedule a call with me!

campaigns.name: Front Desk DDS
campaigns.subject: Important Cyber Security Update: FrontDeskDDS
campaigns.html:
Dear Darkhorse Clients, 

 

I write to you today with an update on a vendor that is practicing less than secure methods to access your office. This vendor is called FrontDeskDDS (Breakaway/Unlimitech/DentalWhale), and we have discovered they are not observing best practices in securing that connection.  

 

Earlier this week, a client was hit with ransomware. Initially we looked at this, thinking it was one of our systems that had allowed this in, however, upon further investigation, the threat came through FrontDeskDDS’ connection to that office. We reviewed the logs and it is certain this was initiated through their networks, and was deposited into that clients’ network. We are working with investigators to determine if this was them being attacked or if it was a disgruntled employee and will provide updates as we have more info. 

 

Our recommendation is to, at minimum, reach out to FrontDeskDDS and ask them to provide proof they have fixed their security issue, or end services with them. If you need a recommendation on a different vendor, please let us know and we can send that to you.  

 

Our goal is to provide you with the best security as possible and prevent things before they happen. 

If you have any questions, our managers can be reached at 800-868-4504 or managers@darkhorsetech.com 

 

Sincerely, 

 

Reuben Kamp 

CEO, Darkhorse Tech

campaigns.html:
Backups.

Where do I start and is my current backup working properly?

This month we are talking about where to start and how to build a proper backup system for your patient’s data.

This is probably the most common request that Darkhorse fields from prospects. There is a lot of confusion in the marketplace, so it is not surprising. Plus, companies wave the word HIPAA around like a magic wand, but don’t actually address the root problem.
 

What is the root problem?

If my server or patient database were to have an issue:

  1. Is my patient health information/database recoverable (tested)?
  2. How long is my downtime (how much production lost)?
  3. Can I access it outside the office (major catastrophe)?

In this article, we will learn where to start, some non-recommended methods, and the experts' preferred method for backups. As IT providers, we want our clients to focus on running their business and not having an itch in the back of their head when they walk in the door about what is going to happen if their server crashes.

Bad Scenario 1: You or your staff are swapping in hard drives daily. You or they are then bringing those hard drives, which contain your entire patient database. PLEASE STOP DOING THIS. This is in fact the worst method. You are one fumble away from having to self-report a breach to the Office of Civil Rights. If this falls us of your purse, bag, or car, and you don’t know where it is, you are legally required to self-report.

Bad Scenario 2: Online Backup Only. Ignoring the local backup and its importance will at some point in your career costs you thousands of dollars in lost wages and production. In this scenario of a system down event, all your data is located on a remote server instead of being quickly accessible on a local system. In order to get it all back, you will rely on how fast your internet speed is. The average dental data set is roughly 500GB, and the average dental internet speed is 200mb/s (shared broadband). This would take approximately 3 days to just download the data set, then there would be another 4-8 hours to get the data in place to serve as a temporary server.  

Bad Scenario 3: I will lump the rest of the scenarios here. It goes like this: yes, my backups are being done, but they have never been tested. Time to stop reading now and go check. A backup that is not tested is in fact not a backup at all.

Have you seen the quote from F. Scott Fitzgerald? “Never confuse a single defeat with a final defeat.” If you have tried options in the past and been burned or less than enthused. Now is not the time to give up.

You might have read up until this point and asked yourself, I think my backup strategy is either lacking, unknown, nonexistent, or failing. Where do I go from here?  The answer is Darkhorse Tech. We have designed a system where you don’t have to think. Our system encompasses all the latest HIPAA, Cybersecurity, and Best Practice Standards out there. For one low monthly cost, we offer two things: Peace of mind, and a Plan in Place.

Patient Education & Engagement in the Waiting Room
Hello!
I wanted to send a quick email to tell you about a brand-new piece of awesome dental tech called Channel D, which is a new video system for the patient lounge. 
 
I first saw it in one of my client's offices in Kansas City. It's simple, clever and patient's actually want to watch it. It doesn't look anything like the other systems. Their angle is also one of comedy, not of lasers cutting through gums. We’re seeing that it's lifting the mood in my client's waiting room. More importantly, this sets the office apart from competitors and is more of a growth tool than just passive education. It also highlights services that they office that their patients never knew about.
 
The setup is just plug and play. The content is all controlled from your account and is WiFi connected so that you'll get access to all the new content. It's much more customized than anything else out there and they'll cleverly integrate photos of you and your team into many of the videos. 
I've contacted Channel D and I've negotiated a deal for all Darkhorse clients.  You'll get 10% off the monthly subscription. ($171 pm instead of $190). They will also send you their media stick for no charge (valued at $138).
 
You can try it for free for 2 months. If you don't want to continue, it will have cost you nothing. It really is different than anything I've seen before. Much more personable and human. I suggest you check it out.  And let me know what you think!

Sincerely,
Reuben Kamp

campaigns.name: End of Life Hardware 2020 (copy 01)
campaigns.subject: SECOND NOTICE: Windows 7 End of Life - Plan for 2020
campaigns.html:
SECOND NOTICE
January 14th is fast approaching! 
Contact us today with questions about how this will affect your practice.
Implementing and learning new software can often be intimidating and overwhelming.  Because of this, many dental offices have delayed switching from Windows 7 to Windows 10.  As many of you may know, Microsoft is ending support for Windows 7 Professional and Server 2008 on January 14th, 2020. When this period ends, Microsoft will discontinue Windows 7 support so that it can focus on investing support on newer technologies. After that, technical assistance and automatic updates that help protect your PC from viruses, malware and attacks will no longer be made available for the product.
So, what does this mean for your practice? This is a major issue for everyone, but especially dental offices because it is an automatic HIPAA violation.  While HIPAA doesn’t explicitly state that running Windows 7 will be a violation, it does express that “procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software” must be in place.  Continuing to run Windows 7 or Server 2008 comes with serious risk to the security of your network, patient information and other sensitive data – not to mention potential penalties down the road.
Our technical team at Darkhorse has details on each computer in your practice and can give guidance on which workstations and servers can be upgraded to Windows 10 Pro, and which will ultimately need to be replaced. While cost of replacing computers is obviously an important concern, there is still roughly a year until support will end. If replacing all of your computers immediately isn’t something you can handle, consider budgeting for a couple computers per month to spread the cost out over time. It’s not too late to start planning for hardware budget now.

Let us help!
 

Reach out to Reuben at sales@darkhorsetech.com or 800-868-4504 to help plan your transition to Windows 10 and Server 2016.
